newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdanski clears merger with BIG.
newsitem.headline: Gdanski clears merger with BIG.

text.p: The shareholders' meeting of Bank Gdanski SA approved a merger with its 63.4 percent owner, Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG), under which one Gdanski share will be exchanged for 10 BIG shares.
The meeting overwhelmingly supported Thursday's decision of BIG to lower the number of its shares offered for one Gdanski share to 10 from the earlier planned 11.

The merger, cleared by 13.3 million in the presence of 14.3 million votes, opens the way for the creation of Poland's fifth biggest bank in terms of capital, which amounted to 866 million zlotys in March.
BIG shareholders on Thursday also approved a new issue of 196,120,000 shares for Gdanski shareholders. After the exchange, shares of Gdanski will be retired.
BIG wants to issue the new shares in September, a move creating an institution with 145 offices in Poland and joint assets of 8.7 billion zlotys.
BIG plans to additionally issue between 60 and 75 million shares before the merger, part of which could be GDRs exchangeable for Gdanski GDRs. Gdanski has 19.5 percent of its shares in GDRs.
The planned merger which already has been cleared by the anti-monopoly office still needs approval from the National Bank of Poland, the central bank.
